children: By George Glover and Mariapaula Gonzalez
Stocks traded higher Monday as technology stocks rebounded from last week's losses ahead of a high-stakes week of earnings, with Meta Platforms, Netflix, and Tesla all set to report.
The artificial-intelligence trade came roaring back Monday. Sandisk, Advanced Micro Devices, Coherent, Corning, Lumentum, Marvell, and Super Micro Computer Inc. rose.

Intel rose 5.9% to $95.18 after J.P. Morgan upgraded the stock to Neutral from Underperform while maintaining a $85 price target, saying the risk/reward for Intel is more balanced with the stock near its price target after falling over 14% last week.
CoreWeave advanced 3.9%. It plummeted 24% last week as yields on its debt soared, rattling investors because of how closely the cloud-computing company's fortunes have been tied to the AI boom.

Tesla added 1.7%. The electric-vehicle maker's shares dropped 2.1% on Friday as even its flying car wasn't enough to lift the AI doom and gloom. Tesla is expected to post third-quarter earnings after the closing bell Wednesday.

SpaceX stock was up 2.4% after Elon Musk said he would give one of his shares in the company to every child in America next year. "This will be the first of many," he said in a post on X. SpaceX is scheduled to report earnings after the closing bell Tuesday.

Amazon rose 2.5% to $256.22. Morgan Stanley raised Amazon's price target to $350 from $335 and made the stock a "top pick." The firm thinks Amazon is a key AI winner even as Meta Platforms' consumer AI agent Muse threatens traditional e-commerce.
Datadog gained 4.2%. Bernstein upgraded the cloud monitoring company to Outperform from Market Perform, saying AI tailwinds will likely boost the stock.

Cleveland-Cliffs climbed 12% after reporting stronger-than-expected guidance for next year. The company expects 2027 adjusted Ebitda to exceed $4 billion, well above Wall Street projections of $2.5 billion. CEO Lourenco Goncalves says 50% tariffs on raw steel have supported the domestic industry by raising prices and reducing imports.
